They will identify connections between their community and other communities (local, national, and global) and will develop an awareness that communities depend on each other to meet their needs and wants. Enrollment in this class is determined by the Assistant Principal of Special Education at Fair Haven Union Middle and High School.
notes: Catalog heading 'US History & Geography I & II'

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: This elective directs the student to an examination of current events and issues in the United States. At least one issue or problem will be explored in each of six areas: political/legal, social, economic, cultural, diplomatic, and environmental. Students will use newspapers and periodicals to study the background, positions, and possible solutions to each issue.

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: The purpose of Particular Topics in Psychology is to help students understand their behavior and the behavior of others in order to strengthen them as individuals and as members of groups. Topics such as basic needs, personality development, and philosophy are introduced in Unit I: Understanding Ourselves. Relationships with others are explored in Unit II.

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: World People Studies introduces students to the elements of culture and culture’s relationship to geographic setting. In addition to examining one’s own culture, students will investigate cultures throughout the world. As a result, students will begin to understand the perspectives of others and respect those who are from cultures that are different from their own. Class presentations are a major component of this course.

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: The focus of this course is the law and some of the many areas in which the law affects our lives. Students successfully completing this course will have a basic understanding of how the law attempts to deal with the problems of American Society. An overview of our legal system, criminal law, and contracts are among the nine topics to be covered.

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
course_name: Intro to Law Enforcement & Public Services
description: Juniors and seniors interested in a possible career in law enforcement, armed forces, or public service should consider taking this introductory-level basic training course that covers motor vehicle law, Doppler radar training, crash investigation, intro. to fish & wildlife, landlord & tenant law, stalking, K9 operations, search & rescue, first aid & CPR, basic finger-printing, crime scene investigation, report writing, and various hands-on practice situations and physical training activities led by our school resource officer.

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: Students will be given the opportunity to receive first hand experiences in the workforce in a field or occupation they choose, through paid and unpaid positions, internships, and job shadowing. Students will learn while working for a more direct approach compared to other courses the school offers by putting them in real life situations while giving them a different perspective on what it takes to be successful while exploring possible careers. In some cases and employment opportunities, students can get a jump start on their career prior to graduating high school to make the transition smooth and effective. Self evaluations, employer feedback, and 2 in-school class days per week will all be used to oversee students progress. Recommended Prior Coursework: Career Exploration and Adulting 101. Students must be enrolled in 4 academic courses unless an exception is approved by an administrator. Students must average 10 work hours per week and submit regular time logs and summaries to earn a full credit per semester. Students must maintain passing grades in all other courses to remain eligible to participate in this course. Students are limited to 2 credits per year.
prerequisites: Career Exploration and Adulting 101.
notes: program

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: This course will introduce students to potential career paths as well as teach them how to identify their strengths, skills and interests. Students in this course will be introduced to careers and jobs both locally and nationally along with college, education, and training required for certain occupations. Students will be exposed to local businesses in the area through field trips, guest speakers, and individual research. Resume building and interview skills will also be covered. As they move on, students will learn about employability skills, ways to find jobs, workplace regulations, and expectations. This class is designed to give students an idea of what is possible after high school as well as the ability to plan their pathway to become successful adults.

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: Students will learn about the attributes of entrepreneurs and research specific business owners to find out more about their paths and success. Innovation & Entrepreneurship asks students to apply their math, science, English, civic, problem-solving and communication skills to real-world dilemmas faced by local employers. Students will create solutions to address employer dilemmas. Then, just as it happens in the real world, students will present their ideas to a panel of “potential investors”. Students will learn how attitudes and behaviors affect entrepreneurs. Students will develop a business plan of their own for a product or service and develop plans for operation, marketing, management and finance. Students will present this plan at the end of this class. Innovation & Entrepreneurship will provide students with experiences at a local manufacturer exposing students to the world of entrepreneurship, design, and manufacturing in the most direct manner possible.

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: “D.U.O.” stands for “Do Unto Others”. It is an educational program that encourages students to become involved in voluntary activity to benefit others. It is a commonly held belief that helping others ultimately helps people learn more and feel good about themselves. Students can arrange DUO in place of a study hall. Students wishing to pursue a DUO project must fill out a DUO application and contract with their DUO sponsor. DUO applications may be obtained from the Guidance Office.
notes: program

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: In this course your student(s) will learn the soft skills needed to be successful in the working world and life after graduation. There will be explicit instruction on steps students need to take in order to apply, obtain, and maintain employment. Students will leave class with a cover letter, resume, and understanding of how to apply for work in the state of Vermont/New York, by the end of the year students will have gained skills to navigate potential employment opportunities. Through a rigorous course structure with outside partnerships and businesses as guest speakers, student(s) will know outside resources, job markets, and make connections throughout this year long course. This course offers a brief counseling on disability disclosure at the workplace. Acceptance will be determined by the Assistant Principal of Special Services. Students must be grade 11 or 12

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: This class offers students a comprehensive intervention program designed to meet the needs of students who require reading support and math support. This class is designed to address student’s academic needs. Enrollment in this course is determined by the Assistant Principal/Director of Special Education. Awarded credit is determined by student’s individualized team.

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: This program focuses on analyzing and repairing structural and non-structural vehicle damage. Students gain experience in mechanical and electrical repair, frame straightening and panel replacement, plastics and adhesives, refinishing techniques and procedures, management and operation of a privately owned auto body business. Embedded Science or Math credit; up to 6 units of credit; Certifications include Axalta Paint, Safety Practices SP2, SEMS Plastic Repair, ICar, and ASE. Articulation agreement with Lincoln Technical Institute.
fulfills_text: Embedded Science or Math credit

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: Students interested in cars should consider this program where they learn how to diagnose and repair vehicles. Stafford’s well-equipped lab provides a valuable opportunity for hands-on learning. Here students develop entry-level skills in the areas of engine performance, engine repair, electrical/electronics, brakes, suspension and steering, automatic transmission/ transaxles, standard transmissions and drive trains, and heating-ventilation-air conditioning (HVAC). As students master these techniques, they also learn more about complex electrical diagnostic procedures using computer systems. Embedded Science or Math credit; up to 6 units of credit; NATEF Certification; multiple college credits available through numerous college partners.
fulfills_text: Embedded Science or Math credit

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: This program offers a strong introduction to the tools and techniques of the industry. Students learn to use hand and power tools safely and accurately, develop project-estimating skills and become familiar with contemporary building materials. Students build with panelization methods. Students gain practical experience from frame to finish on and off-campus at Stafford’s residential project. Embedded Math credit; up to 6 units of credit; OSHA-10 Construction Safety Certification; NCCER Core Curriculum; articulation agreement with New England Institute of Technology.
fulfills_text: Embedded Math credit

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: The Cosmetology curriculum is designed to provide competency-based knowledge, scientific artistic principles, and hands-on fundamentals associated with the Cosmetology industry. Students enroll in the program for potentially two academic years and are expected to accumulate 1,000 program hours required to be eligible for the Vermont state cosmetology licensing exam. Applied academics in the areas of business and finance, cosmetic chemistry, and language arts are an integral part of the program. Embedded Science or Math credit; up to 6 units of credit; Barbicide, OSHA 10, and Cosmetology licensure possible.
fulfills_text: Embedded Science or Math credit

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: In Culinary Arts, students will be provided with a unique opportunity to explore and experience the skills, stamina and education associated with the industry. Students will gain knowledge and training through our on-site bakeshop and restaurant. Our laboratory features some of the newest electric, environmentally friendly technology that is currently available. Practical experiences will include: food safety and food sanitation, food preparation, pastry arts, purchasing, cost analysis, production, fabrication, knife skills, professionalism, marketing, nutrition, and other skills needed to operate a business. Good math skills and physical stamina are essential. Embedded Math or Science credit; Serv/Safe and American Heart Association Heartsaver CPR/AED Certifications; up to 6 units of credit; accelerated status agreement with the New England Culinary Institute.
fulfills_text: Embedded Math or Science credit

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: Digital Arts is a college bound course where students explore graphic design, web and game design, digital photography, illustration, computer animation and fine arts. Students create and communicate through hands-on project based learning. The class will often function as an advertising agency/production house creating materials for the school and local clients. Personal vision and individual artistic aesthetic will be nurtured and encouraged. Curriculum and specific lessons are based on freshman foundation courses at a college of art and design. The assignments will help students develop a strong portfolio of work for the college application and scholarship process. Embedded Art credit and 0.5 credit of Information Technology; up to 6 units of credit; college credit available through the Vermont State College System.
fulfills_text: Embedded Art credit and 0.5 credit of Information Technology

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: The Electrical/Plumbing program will help students develop skills to enter their chosen career though VT Apprenticeship program or continue studies at the College level. The classroom experience is enhanced by on-site practical applications at the residential building project and other electrical or plumbing construction projects in the area. In addition, students have a “hands-on” introduction to applications in Solar and Wind Renewable Energy, Energy Conservation, HVAC, Blueprint Reading, and Electrical/Plumbing/HVAC System Design. Embedded Science or Math credit; up to 6 units of credit; OSHA Construction Safety and American Heart Association Heartsaver CPR/AED certifications; NCCER Construction Core; Year 1 State Apprenticeship for Electrical & Plumbing. Articulation agreement with Lincoln Technical Institute.
fulfills_text: Embedded Science or Math credit

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: A firm grasp of Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) is essential for success in today’s highly skilled global economy. The Engineering program incorporates advanced technologies through project-based learning. Through the nationally recognized Project Lead the Way Pathway to Engineering program, students will apply the design process and acquire strong teamwork, communication, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills. Students gain valuable experience working with fundamental engineering principles and applied physics, advanced manufacturing, 3D printing, laser cutting, robotics and machine tools. The course of studies includes Introduction to Engineering Design, Computer Integrated Manufacturing, Principles of Engineering and Digital Electronics. Embedded Math or Science as well as 0.5 Information Technology or 0.5 Fine Art credits. Up to 6 units of credit recommended in Engineering, Math, Science, Information Technology, and Art; Autodesk Fusion 360 Certified User and American Heart Association Heartsaver CPR/AED, OSHA 10, Conover Workplace Readiness Certifications. Dual enrollment college credits available through New Hampshire Institute of Technology.
credits_text: Up to 6 units of credit recommended in Engineering, Math, Science, Information Technology, and Art
fulfills_text: Embedded Math or Science as well as 0.5 Information Technology or 0.5 Fine Art credits

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: Through a partnership with Castleton State College, Southern Vermont Area Health Education Center and Rutland Regional Medical Center, our new Health Careers Academy provides an in-depth, two-year program, combining classroom learning with hands-on practice in a wide variety of health care environments. Year One focuses on observation, guest speakers, and hands-on learning experiences. Year Two emphasizes continued coursework and clinical experiences. Embedded credit in Social Studies or Family and Consumer Science (FACS). Certifications include Basic Life Saving with AED, First Aid, Stop the Bleed, and Licensed Nursing Assistant. Potential for college credits through dual enrollment and other courses; several college partners.
fulfills_text: Embedded credit in Social Studies or Family and Consumer Science (FACS)

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: Students explore physical, intellectual, emotional and social development throughout the life cycle. Students will explore and develop the skills, mindset, cultural competence, and growth mindset necessary to be in education. Students will expand interpersonal skills, focus on communication issues and explore problem-solving, leadership and teamwork skill-building. Fieldwork includes service in the preschool lab and at various community agencies. Students learn to strengthen personal relationships and workplace skills. This is a reading and writing intensive program and strong comprehension skills are necessary. Embedded credit in Social Studies or Family and Consumer Studies (FACS); up to 6 units of credit; Certifications include American Heart Association Pediatric CPR/AED with First Aid, VT Mandated Reporter, Penn State Better Kid Care, Prevent child Abuse VT Shaken Baby. Potential college credits through several college partners.
fulfills_text: Embedded credit in Social Studies or Family and Consumer Studies (FACS)

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: This program helps students interested in conservation and natural resource management gain skills, knowledge and experience while developing valuable relationships with industry professionals. Students will be involved in practical experiences related to forest ecology, outdoor recreation, wildlife and fisheries science, soil and water quality analysis and conversation, heavy equipment operation, landscape installation and conservation-related construction projects. The natural areas of western Vermont become the lab as students explore working forests, observation and recreational areas, nurseries and farms, and processing facilities. Embedded Science or Math credit. Certifications include Game of Logging 1-2 and OSHA Agricultural Safety. College agreements with Paul Smith’s College and Unity College.
fulfills_text: Embedded Science or Math credit

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: This program has been developed through a partnership between Stafford Technical Center and the Rutland City Police Dept., Vermont State Police, Rutland City Sheriff Dept., Police Academy, Correctional Academy, College of Saint Joseph, and the Rutland Regional Ambulance Service. This program provides students with an introduction and overview of law enforcement careers and crime prevention skills. Students learn through a variety of methods including: classroom lectures, demonstrations, and practical experiences. Embedded Social Studies, Civics or Science credit and 0.5 credit of Health; up to 8 units of credit; Certifications include Incident Command and American Heart Association Heartsaver CPR/AED. College dual enrollment credits possible.
fulfills_text: Embedded Social Studies, Civics or Science credit and 0.5 credit of Health

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: This course introduces students to careers that require visual storytelling such as a video journalist, camera operator, television/film producer and director, video editor, and on-camera talent such as an actor or news reporter. Students work as part of a professional production crew, write scripts, storyboards, shoot and edit projects that appear on local television, and work closely with organizations and businesses in the community. Students film live video productions, produce short films, and create commercials for community non-profits and other clients. Students work with state-of-the-art equipment including High Definition cameras, editing software, and audio recording devices. Students who participate in this program are given the necessary tools to succeed in college and in the professional world. Video Internships are available upon request. Embedded Science; up to 6 units of credit; Certifications earned include Conover Workplace Readiness, WorkKeys Career Readiness, Tier 2 IRC for Media Arts through State of Vermont. College credits available through numerous college partners.
fulfills_text: Embedded Science

school_name: Fair Haven Union Middle and High School
description: Students will learn how to identify and properly use hand tools, power tools, and general welding shop equipment, how to set up and operate SMAW welding equipment, select electrodes and weld in various positions. They will learn how to weld a pad of beads, fillet welds, and groove welds in various positions leading to an AWS welding certification. Students will also be introduced to sheet metal fabrication and light structural fabrication through project-based learning. Students gain experience in diesel technology and have guided practice in the latest metal fabrication equipment, including plasma cutting, GMAW (Gas Metal Arc Welding), SMAW (Stick Metal Arc Welding), TIG (Tungsten Inert Gas) and Oxy-Acetylene welding techniques. Embedded Math or Science credit. Certifications include American Welding Society AWS and OSHA Construction Safety. Potential for college credit through numerous technical and public colleges.
fulfills_text: Embedded Math or Science credit

description: In Language Arts 9, students will develop their skills in reading, writing, speaking, and listening, emphasizing in-class discussion as well as discussion in digital spaces. Full-class and individual explorations will include rigorous engagement with traditional and non-traditional texts from many genres: short story, poetry, drama, novel, memoir, and narrative nonfiction. As students reflect verbally and in writing on selected texts and the big ideas from those texts, they will become more facile with core Language Arts skills and will be ready to move into the more challenging work required in later Language Arts courses.
fulfills_text: Required for 9th Graders
notes: Heading: Language Arts 9 (Year-long); required for graduation (or RVTC Pre Tech)

description: Students in this course will study universal themes in world literature, both classic masterpieces and contemporary works. To supplement their reading, students will study the culture and context of their authors, characters, and themes. In addition, they will analyze, interpret, and evaluate the literary works in terms of genre, purpose, and aesthetic value. In conjunction with their reading, students will produce at least quarterly formal essays demonstrating proficiency in argumentative, informative, and narrative writing. To further address proficiencies students will also develop their skills in grammar, usage, and mechanics. They will also expand their thinking, speaking, listening skills through a variety of class discussions, activities, products, and performances. Requirements for this class include a willingness to read literature from other places and times and to commit to work conscientiously in class on individual and group assignments.
fulfills_text: Required for all 10th Graders

description: This class will cover a representative survey of American Literature, including both classic and contemporary pieces. We will begin with American Literature’s formative roots and trace the changes and modifications that occurred with romanticism, realism, modernism, and postmodernism. The course will deal with the different forms of literature, including poetry, dramas, short stories, novels, and nonfiction essays. Rhetoric and argument will also be covered, along with reflective writing. This course will emphasize critical reading and listening skills, as well as effective development of ideas through the writing process. American ideas about wilderness and nature as a spiritual escape, the conflicts that arise between conformity to society and individual moral responsibility, and art as an instrument of social transformation will be traced and considered in the light of the various works we cover. Students should expect to read and write extensively. Prerequisite: Successful completion of Language Arts 10.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Language Arts 10.
fulfills_text: An American Literature course is required for graduation

description: The AP English Language and Composition course focuses on the development and revision of evidence-based analytic and argumentative writing, the rhetorical analysis of nonfiction and fiction texts, and the decisions writers make as they compose and revise. Students evaluate, synthesize, and cite research to support their arguments. Additionally, they read and analyze rhetorical elements and their effects in nonfiction and fiction texts—including images as forms of text— from a range of disciplines and historical periods. In addition to individual reading and writing, students will undertake preparation for collaborative discussions, research, individual presentations within the context of the class, and critique in support of other learners. Readings will be drawn from diverse time periods, cultures, and subject areas. Readings may be adapted to areas of interest when appropriate. Prerequisite: Students taking this course are required to have successfully completed Language Arts 9 and 10. This course will meet the requirements for American Literature as well and is open to both juniors and seniors. Students are required to take the AP Exam in May.
prerequisites: Students taking this course are required to have successfully completed Language Arts 9 and 10.
fulfills_text: This course will meet the requirements for American Literature as well

description: AP English Literature and Composition offers the student an opportunity to complete college-level studies while still in high school. Depending on the school, students may gain college credit while fulfilling their regular, high school requirements. This course includes an intensive study of representative works from various genres, cultures, and periods, concentrating on works of recognized literary merit. Through the close reading of selected texts, the AP student will deepen their understanding of the ways writers use language to provide both meaning and pleasure for their readers. The student will consider such linguistic choices as a work's structure, style, and themes, as well as such smaller scale elements as the use of figurative language, imagery, symbolism, and tone. In addition to considering a work's literary artistry, careful attention to both textual detail and historical context will provide a broader foundation for interpretation. Because of the intense concentration on language in this course, the successful student will enhance their ability to use grammatical conventions both appropriately and with sophistication, as well as developing a stylistic maturity as a writer. Prerequisite: Students taking this course are required to have successfully completed Language Arts 9 and 10. This course will meet the requirements for American Literature and is open to both juniors and seniors. Students are required to take the AP Exam in May.
prerequisites: Students taking this course are required to have successfully completed Language Arts 9 and 10.
fulfills_text: This course will meet the requirements for American Literature

description: Students in this course will study ethics, current affairs, personal and professional writing, and self-selected topics through the lens of classic literature and contemporary works. They will analyze, interpret, and evaluate texts with regard to authorial intent, bias, audience, and moral principles and refine their skills in analytical writing, research methods, public speaking, and personal and professional writing. Requirements for this class include: a willingness to read literature from other places and times, a commitment to working conscientiously in class, and an openness to considering others’ points of view.

Wilderness literature is an exploration of primitive skills, literature, and nature. This is a hands-on field based course that will cover a variety of topics related to adventure, awareness, primitive skills, and survival. The concept of “wilderness” will be used as a medium for the exploration of nature in literature as it pertains to the self, community, environment, and myth. Participants in the class will be expected to work cooperatively with other students and participate in the class activities. Additional activities such as backpacking and canoe trips may be offered. Be prepared to get dirty, have some fun and experience what wilderness is all about.

This course is designed to allow students to develop an understanding of how to use functions to model and interpret everyday situations. Emphasis is put on linear functions in a variety of representations, while quadratic and exponential functions are also introduced. There will be many opportunities to apply collective mathematical knowledge to solve problems that arise in everyday life, critique information encountered in everyday life, make inferences to decide what conclusions can be drawn about a situation and propose/defend predictions about what will happen in various circumstances. Students will also learn to evaluate their level of motivation to improve proficiency in math knowledge and develop plans to grow that knowledge.
fulfills_text: Students must take Algebra 1, Algebra 2, Geometry, Personal Finance.

description: Algebra II can be hard but enjoyable work. You will use both traditional methods and technology (graphing calculators and computers) to solve increasingly challenging problems and will develop a powerful algebraic understanding. You will increase your ability to understand data, graphs and formulas, and learn to translate among them. You will learn more interesting functions and powerful methods to solve them, including exponential, logarithmic, polynomial, rational, and radical functions. You will become more capable of evaluating and improving your own work and the work of your peers. A strong work ethic significantly increases ability to achieve proficiency in this course. While each post­secondary institution has its own entrance criteria, proficiency in Algebra II is a necessary criterion for the majority of colleges and universities.
fulfills_text: Students must take Algebra 1, Algebra 2, Geometry, Personal Finance.

description: Geometry introduces geometric reasoning as a method for problem solving. In this course, you will explore the properties of geometric figures such as triangles, quadrilaterals, and other polygons. Some important geometric ideas such as symmetry, similarity, and trigonometry will also be examined. Lastly, you will begin to explore the basis of formal mathematical proofs and solid geometry. The course material progresses from more visual, intuitive ways of solving problems to more formal explorations of geometric ideas, properties, and proofs.
fulfills_text: Students must take Algebra 1, Algebra 2, Geometry, Personal Finance.

description: Students who complete this course will have experienced the skills and concepts that are prerequisites for most college calculus courses. Special attention is given to systems of equations, inequalities, exponential and logarithmic functions, polynomial and rational functions, and trigonometric functions. These various concepts will be explored using numerical, algebraic and graphical representations as well as in real world problem solving.

Learning to make sound financial decisions is one of the most important lessons a student can learn. In this course, students will learn financial decision-making skills using real-life applications and data. This course focuses on budgeting, purchasing power, the power of interest, taxes, credit, insurance, investing, growing wealth and philanthropy. These topics will help the student learn to make decisions and have practical skills that will enable them to implement personal decision-making choices; to become wise, successful, and knowledgeable consumers, savers, investors, users of credit and money managers; and to be participating members of a global workforce and society.
fulfills_text: Students must take Algebra 1, Algebra 2, Geometry, Personal Finance.
notes: Required for Class of 2028 onward per graduation requirements ('addition of Personal Finance and Environmental Science')

description: Students who complete this course will learn how to produce good data. They will learn to determine if there is bias present in a particular sampling method. They will also learn how to interpret standard deviation, correlation and confidence intervals related to different data distributions. In addition, the students will be able to determine which statistical summary to use based on the shape of the data distribution. The probability portion of the course will focus on permutations, combinations, and conditional probability. The students will use these concepts to interpret and create probability models.

Calculus is a course in single ­variable calculus that includes techniques and applications of the derivative, techniques and applications of the definite integral, and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. It is equivalent to at least a semester of calculus at most colleges and universities. Algebraic, numerical, and graphical representations are emphasized throughout the course, so students might better appreciate the connections among various representations; it is assumed that they will have access to graphing calculators in class and on homework. To that end, and to shift the emphasis from mere computation to a deeper understanding of concepts, graphing calculators are required on portions of the AP Examination. Prerequisite: Successful completion of Pre-Calculus & Trigonometry significantly increases ability to achieve proficiency in this course. Students will be eligible to take the AP Calculus Exam.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Pre-Calculus & Trigonometry significantly increases ability to achieve proficiency in this course.
notes: Description says students will be eligible to take the AP Calculus Exam

description: This course explores the economic, political, cultural, and social developments in world history before 1500 in Asia, Africa, Europe and the Middle East. The course highlights issues in geography, trade, religious and cultural movements, and social political changes that influenced the historical development of various world societies and their interrelationships within a global context.
fulfills_text: To graduate students are required to successfully complete all proficiencies in World History I, II, United States History, Civics and one year of a foreign language.

description: This course explores the economic, political, cultural, and social developments in world history from 1500 to the present in Asia, Africa, Europe, Oceania, the Middle East, and the Americas. The course highlights issues in geography, trade, religious and cultural movements, and social political changes that influenced the historical development of various world societies and their interrelationships within a global context.
fulfills_text: To graduate students are required to successfully complete all proficiencies in World History I, II, United States History, Civics and one year of a foreign language.

description: Students will study the foundations of American democracy and the origins of American government. Emphasis is placed on the Constitution and the rights and responsibilities of citizens in a democratic society. In addition, the roles of political parties, campaigns & elections, public opinion, and the media will also be considered.
fulfills_text: To graduate students are required to successfully complete all proficiencies in World History I, II, United States History, Civics and one year of a foreign language.

description: U.S. History examines the development and changes of American History from the Industrial Revolution through the War on Terror. The course covers the social, political, cultural, military, economic and diplomatic aspects of various time periods. Students will be expected to compare, contrast, construct, argue, evaluate, infer, deduce, analyze, interpret, criticize, apply, synthesize, explain, justify, summarize, revise, write, and test.
fulfills_text: To graduate students are required to successfully complete all proficiencies in World History I, II, United States History, Civics and one year of a foreign language.

description: Students learn the analytic skills and factual knowledge necessary to deal critically with the problems and materials in U.S. History. Students learn to assess historical materials, their relevance to a given interpretive problem, reliability and importance, and to weigh the evidence and interpretations presented in historical scholarship. The course develops the skills necessary to arrive at conclusions on the basis of an informed judgment and to present reasons and evidence clearly and persuasively in essay format. The course is a survey of the major developments in American history from the end of the Reconstruction Era to the present. Students will trace the social, economic, political, and cultural forces that have shaped the history of the United States to the present day. Emphasizes understanding of contemporary issues in light of our past. Students are expected to take the AP US History Exam.

Students who take this course will study how humans interact within society. As humans we all are involved in society with the formation of groups and institutions that dominate our world. The study of sociology will start with the roots of sociology and examine key issues that concern sociologists: sexuality, gender, race, class, religion and globalization. Throughout the course you will question the reality you live in and just what your role is in society. This course will involve the development of your own sociological studies/projects.

Students in this course will explore the indigenous cultures of North America. The scope of our study includes pre-European civilizations, the history of contact and conflict between natives, conquistadors in the south and English in New England, missionaries, and general settlers in the colonial era. Students will consider native attempts at assimilation and resistance, and national programs aimed at removal, and re-education of natives. Current issues will also be addressed in this course with possible guest speakers. College credits will be awarded from Community College of Vermont upon successful completion of this course.
notes: No grade levels stated

description: Students in Introduction to Psychology will earn 3 college credits upon successful completion of this course. The course focuses on fundamental facts and principles of psychology within the context of contemporary personal and social concerns. Topics in this course may include, the evolution of psychology as a science, human development, motivational theory, consciousness, sensation and perception, learning, thinking, memory, emotions, biological basis of behavior, personality theory, psychopathology and more. Most importantly, students will gain a better understanding of why they and others feel and act the way they do, and are better able to understand, articulate and control their own emotions. Academic skills in this course include reading, writing and discussion at the college level, important skills for college bound students. College credits will be awarded from River Valley Community College upon successful completion of this course.

Students will explore how food shapes and impacts the individual and culture. Students will consider how personal identity and social groups are formed through food production, preparation, and consumption. We will study current political, social, economic and environmental topics around large-scale international agribusiness and local organic farming. The class will prepare and eat various dishes, will travel to local farms, a private school and a Foodbank. As a group, we will develop and implement a service-learning project around food.

This course will explore the sociopolitical factors that make people vulnerable to misinformation and conspiracy theories and the reasons that corrections so often fail to change their minds. We will look at how conspiratorial fears and political paranoia permeates through modern American culture and analyze how these tendencies are exploited by political elites.

description: Integrated Science is an exploration of the systems that characterize the earth, the solar system, and the universe, and the forces that affect and shape those systems over time. It introduces major topics of physical geology, weather, volcanism, earthquakes, and plate tectonics. It also introduces concepts in astronomy including the Big Bang Theory, the chemical makeup of stars, and the evolution of stars. The topics to be covered may vary from year to year based on student interest.

Biology is a foundational science that studies life in its many forms. Spoiler alert: what we call “life” is really just a bunch of dead things coming together in crazy ways. All life on earth, from individual bacteria to global ecosystems has predictable patterns based on fundamental concepts of evolution, heredity, cellular systems, and energy use. Scientific skills such as experimentation, data collection/analysis, and basic laboratory techniques will be introduced and practiced through application of biological concepts in hands-on activities, exploration, and discussion.

Chemistry is the study of matter and the changes it can undergo. This course begins with a general knowledge of matter, its properties, and the techniques necessary to measure and classify it. Additional topics include data analysis, structure of the atom, electron structure, periodic table, chemical bonding, stoichiometry, reaction rate, and chemical equilibrium. The format of the class includes problem solving, laboratory exercises, and analysis. This course is recommended for any student that plans to attend college.

Have you ever wanted to roll a bowling ball down the hall? How about shooting marbles off the steps so they land exactly where you want them to? What about building a projectile launcher? If the answer is yes, then Physics is the class for you. Physics is a course that explores the laws that govern matter in the physical world. We will examine the principles of motion and Newton’s Laws, momentum, energy, heat, and fluid dynamics in problem-based, conceptual, and experimental formats. After completing this course you will have a greater understanding of how matter behaves in the universe. Students will apply mathematical concepts and measurement to solve problems in theoretical and laboratory settings. Recommended: successful completion of Algebra I, Algebra II.
notes: Recommended: successful completion of Algebra I, Algebra II.

description: This course is intended to provide an introduction to modern methods used in detection, investigation and crime lab functions. Students will learn how DNA fingerprinting, footprints, tire tracks, blood splatter and other forensic tests can be used to solve a crime. The learning strategies will include lectures, labs, research, activities and videos. Upon completion, students will have a broader understanding of criminology, laboratory procedures and its function in modern day society. Students will be expected to complete readings, write reports, and complete other assignments in a timely manner.

This class will explore the natural world and our place in it by focusing on the scientific processes and human context that influences our natural resources and the ecological services they provide. Topics will include pollution, conservation, sustainability, and both active and passive resource management. Core understandings will be how environmental set points shift over time and how local perspectives and scientific knowledge about the environment combine to inform policies around use and conservation.
notes: Graduation requirements state 'Environmental Science will be required for students beginning with the Class of 2028'; catalog lists no course by that exact name

description: This is an advanced placement course designed to prepare the student for the AP Chemistry exam. The course covers the equivalent of one full year of college level General Chemistry, comparable to a first year course at a college or university. The course is a rigorous math-based course with a strong laboratory component. It is intended for students who have demonstrated a willingness to commit considerable time to studying and completing assignments outside of class, and who have successfully completed a prior course in chemistry during high school. Since passing the AP exam may qualify the student to bypass a first-year college chemistry course, AP Chemistry should not be considered “college prep.” Rather, this is a college class, with college level expectations for behavior, participation and effort. Prerequisite: Successful completion of Chemistry and Algebra II (or currently enrolled) or permission from the instructor. Students are required to take the AP Exam at the end of the course.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Chemistry and Algebra II (or currently enrolled) or permission from the instructor.
offering_note: Will be offered the following school year 2025-26.

description: This advanced biology course is for students who think humans are fascinating biological organisms. Students planning a career in medicine, allied health or physical education are encouraged to enroll. We will focus on the different organ systems and how they work. While some memorization is necessary, this course will provide students with a vast array of ways to learn. There will be some lectures, videos, guest speakers, etc. along with a strong laboratory component. Students will do multiple dissections of specific organs as well as a whole animal dissection at the end of the course. While not mandatory, the dissections are strongly encouraged. Prerequisite: Successful completion of Biology.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Biology.

description: This course is designed to be the equivalent to a college introductory biology course. The College Board dictates the scope of this course. It differs substantially from the usual biology course in rigor, range, and depth. Students will use a college level textbook, as well as lectures and in depth laboratories. AP Biology aims to provide students with the conceptual framework, factual knowledge, and analytical skills necessary to deal critically with the rapidly changing field of biology. Topics included but not limited to molecules and cells, heredity and evolution, organisms and ecological populations. Students are required to take the AP Exam at the end of the course. Prerequisites: Successful completion of Biology, and approval by AP Biology teacher. Chemistry is highly recommended. Offered 2026-27 school year
prerequisites: Successful completion of Biology, and approval by AP Biology teacher. Chemistry is highly recommended.

description: This is a project-based science course designed to give students experience applying scientific concepts by designing and conducting experiments in various fields of science including physics, chemistry, ecology, and biology. Topics of study will cover a wide range of real world issues and related science content, and can be individualized to meet student interests. These might include things such as global climate change, advanced laboratory experimentation, field research, citizen science projects, or engineering projects. Students will learn new content or expand on previous knowledge through a process that includes: observation and research, developing testable questions, designing and conducting experiments and projects, analyzing data, and sharing results. Because of the flexible nature of this course, it is appropriate for any student that can work independently and is self motivated. This includes students wanting to expand their knowledge past the AP science classes to others who may be learning the content for the first time. This course will cover each of the required science proficiencies. 9th Graders must get approval from the current science teacher and instructor.
fulfills_text: This course will cover each of the required science proficiencies.

description: Students dig deep into the engineering design process, applying math, science, and engineering standards to hands-on projects. Intro to Engineering is a continuation of the STEM 7 Design and Modeling and the STEM 8 Automation and Robotics courses. In the Design and Modeling portion of the course, students will create and test different Toy prototypes in order to meet specific design requirements. In the Automation and Robotics section, students build robots to meet a survival challenge and then learn to code robots to perform various tasks using different sensors. Students work both individually and in teams to design solutions to a variety of problems using 3-D modeling software, and use an engineering notebook to document their work. This course is designed for students who have little or no experience with the Engineering Design Process.

Wilderness Adventures is an exploration of primitive skills, philosophy, and nature. This is a hands-on field based course that will cover a variety of topics related to adventure, awareness, primitive skills, and survival. The concept of “wilderness” will be used as a medium for the exploration of nature in literature as it pertains to the self, community, environment, and myth. Emphasis will be placed on “experiencing” much of the material covered in class, and therefore most of the classes will be conducted in the forest behind GMUHS. Participants in the class will be expected to work cooperatively with other students and participate in the class activities. Additional activities such as backpacking and canoe trips may be offered. Be prepared to get dirty, have some fun and experience what wilderness is all about.

This course is designed to offer students a basic understanding of the uses of art/design-based software and programs used in graphic arts, primarily Adobe and iPad software such as ProCreate. Students will explore art, design and careers using the computer as a means of production. Topics include Logo Design, Publication and Typographic Design, and Advertising and Marketing Design. A foundation in the elements and principles of art will be established and applied to computer generated art using the iPad and PhotoShop as well.
notes: Visual Arts

description: Explore the many facets and capabilities of the digital camera as well as some of the enhancement possibilities PhotoShop and other programs can achieve. It is designed as an introduction to concepts in photography and an exploration of digital photography in the world today.
notes: Visual Arts

description: Explore a variety of comic, cartoon and illustration drawing styles and techniques in this introductory course. Over the duration of this course, you will experiment with character design, drawing and inking techniques, creating an environment, plot development, and producing a finished comic. We will explore different styles of comics and cartoons including DC, Marvel, anime, Disney and much more. Students will also learn the fundamentals of drawing and illustration, keeping a sketchbook to track their growth and skills they learn along the way. We will explore many styles and applications of illustration such as narrative, decorative, informative and conceptual illustration categories. We will use traditional materials as well as the iPad Pro as a means of production. Student interests will drive much of the content of the curriculum once fundamental skills, techniques and styles are introduced and practiced.
notes: Visual Arts

description: We will build on your drawing skills and basic understanding of art through printmaking, collage, bookmaking, experimental techniques, mixed media & recycled material arts and crafts, fiber arts, sewing and embroidery. This course will expand upon the elements and principles of design, while incorporating art history, self-reflection and unique projects.
notes: Visual Arts

description: In this beginner level course, students will be introduced to the basic elements of visual art as they apply to two-dimensional design. Lessons and projects will thoroughly cover the areas of line, shape, color, value, texture, form, space and composition; and will explore a wide variety of materials to include pencil, charcoal, pastels, colored pencil, marker, watercolor pencil, liquid watercolor paint and acrylic paint. Students will become familiar with common, important art vocabulary; study certain artists and periods of art history, learn to professionally present their work through cropping and matting, and complete the course with a unique collection of personal artwork and a general understanding of the world of 2D art.
notes: Visual Arts

description: Creative Arts is a course that will allow you to explore areas of visual art that are a bit outside the typical drawing and painting projects. Assignments will explore ideas and techniques centered around building on your drawing skills and basic understanding of art through printmaking, collage, bookmaking, experimental techniques, mixed media recycled material arts and crafts, to name a few! This course will expand upon the elements and principles of design, while incorporating modern art history, self-reflection and unique projects.
notes: Visual Arts

description: Students explore ceramic art by practicing hand-building techniques, such as pinching and coiling. The design and creation of utilitarian pieces is emphasized; students learn balance and proportion, wall thickness correction, surface decoration techniques and new firing options.This course teaches students the fundamental wheel-working skills used for shaping clay. Students practice using the potter's wheel and begin throwing basic forms, such as bowls, mugs, vases and creative art forms.
notes: Visual Arts

description: This painting class will deeply explore the world of painting through the use of acrylic, watercolor, and pastels. Students will strongly focus on color theory, color mixing, brush choice, use of materials and supplies, and a variety of painting techniques; as well as the important principles of composition, contrast, movement, emphasis, rhythm and balance in creating art. Students will draw inspiration from artists throughout history and the artwork they created, as well as from nature, still-life, wildlife, landscapes and portraiture. They will also be encouraged to illustrate their own voice and develop a personal style. Students will actively create a portfolio of their work to document their growth and learning throughout the course and will learn to professionally present work.
notes: Visual Arts

description: In Drawing & Illustration, students will fine tune their drawing and sketching skills by expanding upon their knowledge of line, value, composition, and realism by working with a variety of drawing materials on multiple assignments. Materials will likely include drawing pencils, charcoal, specialty papers, pen & ink, colored pencil, pastels, illustration markers, and drawing pens. Lessons will include still-life and drawing from life, portraiture (to include self-portraits), nature journaling, creating 2D texture, and perspective, to name a few.
notes: Visual Arts

description: Students will learn the most important and foundational skills of carpentry. This includes the basics of four-view drawing, measurement, fastening techniques, proper hand and power tool usage; as well as demonstrating proficiency in square, level, plumb and straight. Students in this class will research, design, draw and build their own projects as well as having the opportunity to do other projects for the school and community.
notes: Visual Arts

description: Students who complete this course will establish safe and productive work habits in the shop. They will also be proficient in hand, portable, and stationary tool use. Each student will complete one or more cabinet grade projects. Students will be able to design projects to meet their needs. Students will also learn advanced joining and finishing techniques. Prerequisite: Successful completion of Woodworking.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Woodworking.
notes: Visual Arts

description: Wood Carving and Whittling are ancient forms of artistic creativity that combine art, sculpting and woodworking into a beautiful vocation and life-long hobby. This course will introduce and teach proper safety, techniques and tooling necessary to do several different types of wood carvings such as; whittling, caricatures, spoon carving, relief carving, and even some power carving. These projects can also be combined with pieces of furniture and woodworking projects to make a project really stand out.
notes: Visual Arts

description: Choral students rehearse and perform a variety of musical literature composed by past and contemporary composers. We give various choral performances throughout the year, both in school as well as in the community. The ensemble sings in 3-4 part harmonies and covers a variety of genres. Participants are required to perform in all performances and encouraged to audition for music festivals at the district and state level.
notes: Performing Arts

description: Band is a comprehensive study, through rehearsal and performance, of quality musical literature of both traditional and contemporary styles. Students will have the opportunity to perform outside of school in concert and marching settings. Participants are required to take part in performances and are encouraged to audition for and participate in music festivals at the district and/or state level.
notes: Performing Arts

description: Health Education provides students with the knowledge and skills they need to maintain health and wellness throughout their lifetime. The intent of a comprehensive health education program is to motivate students to improve their health, prevent disease, and avoid or reduce health related risk behaviors. All teaching and learning is focused on student achievement of learning proficiencies. Health education provides real life learning experiences with personal applications of scientifically research-based health knowledge and skills in relevant situations. Health Education creates opportunities and experiences that engage and challenge our students to assess, explore, and question their health, while personalizing, adapting and evaluating their learning.
fulfills_text: Students need to take the following courses in order to meet the graduation requirements: Health I and Physical Education I; Health II and Physical Education II

description: Physical Education is a comprehensive course that includes many different types of physical activities, including individual, dual activities and team sports including basketball, soccer, ultimate frisbee, football, disc golf, softball, weight room, badminton, pickleball, and lawn sports. This class requires students to be active in class every day. For this Physical Education course, a complete change of clothes is encouraged to participate and non-marking athletic shoes are required. This course covers required enduring graduation standards.
fulfills_text: Students need to take the following courses in order to meet the graduation requirements: Health I and Physical Education I; Health II and Physical Education II

description: Personal Health and Wellness is based around improving one’s overall, well rounded health and level of wellness through a variety of health enhancing learning activities. The students will spend time in the classroom learning different ways to exercise, fitness techniques, aspects of healthy nutrition, CPR/ First Aid, Advocacy, and will address other health topics as well.
prerequisites: HE 9
fulfills_text: Students need to take the following courses in order to meet the graduation requirements: Health I and Physical Education I; Health II and Physical Education II

description: Prerequisite: PE 9 Students will spend time working on their personal fitness. They will apply techniques they learn by creating and implementing their own personalized fitness plans in order to achieve personal goals. Students will also participate in team sports and individual and dual activities. For this Physical Education course, a complete change of clothes is encouraged to participate and non-marking athletic shoes are required. This class requires students to be active in class every day. This course covers required enduring graduation standards.
prerequisites: PE 9
fulfills_text: Students need to take the following courses in order to meet the graduation requirements: Health I and Physical Education I; Health II and Physical Education II

description: TRSU offers the opportunity for our students to take courses online through Vermont Virtual Learning Cooperative (VTVLC) and Brigham Young University (BYU). Students should be independent learners and self starters. Full course descriptions for both programs are available on their website at www.vtvlc.org. Since there are limited seats available in these programs, please make sure to speak to your Guidance Counselor and reference it on your course selection sheet. There are additional steps needed to sign up for online courses. Online courses meet in the Flexible Pathways classroom and are part of the students regular daily schedule.
notes: program

course_name: Dual Enrollment and Early College Opportunities
description: ACT 77’s Flexible Pathways is a wonderful opportunity for students to take college courses while still in high school. We encourage and support students in this endeavor. Students are eligible for two free dual enrollment classes once they complete their sophomore year. Students also have the opportunity to participate in Early College which allows students to do their senior year taking courses at local colleges. Students should reach out to their guidance counselor and/or our Flexible Pathways Coordinator if they are interested in pursuing these opportunities.
notes: program; Act 77 Flexible Pathways

course_name: Dartmouth College's Special Community Student Program
description: Students who have exceeded course offerings at TRSU are also able to participate in Dartmouth College’s Special Community Student Program. This program enables high school juniors and seniors to take a regular Dartmouth College course at no expense; however, they need to provide their own transportation. Courses are offered on a trimester basis; August, November, and February. The process of signing up is complicated and requires that you set up an appointment with your Guidance Counselor to discuss the details weeks before the semester starts.
notes: program; grades from description 'high school juniors and seniors'

description: Community Based Learning provides students a learning-by-doing experience utilizing the community as an extension of the classroom. CBL experiences add authenticity to learning by affording supervised, real-world experiences to students eager to explore vocational and avocational interests. Through the mentoring provided by community partners, students’ worlds expand beyond high school walls; their perspectives on themselves as engaged learners, young adults, and responsible community members change and mature. In CBL’s, students accumulate evidence for the Transferable Skills proficiencies. Should a student choose to seek additional content-specific proficiencies, those proficiencies will need to be planned through their advisor, the content department, and the guidance department.
notes: program

description: Students must hold a valid Learner's Permit before the start of the courses. It is a requirement for Driver Education. The Driver Education course is designed to familiarize the student with the operation and care of the automobile. The safe operation of the automobile and defensive driving tactics will be stressed. The use of the Zone Control System for precision driving will be used as a supplementary driving guide. The correct use of the 5 lane positions and reference points will be covered. This class meets before school for 12 weeks. Additional observation and driving time is also required. You must sign up with the Guidance Office, as enrollment for this course is limited. Preference is given to students based on date of birth.
notes: Meets before school for 12 weeks; Learner's Permit required
